alternatives: Telephone survey with self-reported ownership (refused: low renter response and overstated prevalence)
Analysis of fire service visit records (refused: visits are made on request)
Cluster randomised trial of proactive alarm fitting (refused: the prevalence question comes first)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial of proactive fitting would need the prevalence map this survey produces; a panel design is unnecessary for a one-off targeting decision.
rationale: The question is a prevalence estimate with a comparison between tenure groups at one point in time, which is what a cross-sectional survey measures. Renters are already known to be four times less likely to have a working alarm, so the survey mainly confirms the size of the problem.

decision.statement: Run the door-to-door survey this winter because renters are four times less likely than owners to have a working carbon monoxide alarm (claim-9).
decision.question: Should the health unit run a door-to-door cross-sectional survey of working alarms by tenure this winter?

criteria.text: Renters are four times less likely than owners to have a working carbon monoxide alarm.

gates.requirement: Research ethics committee decision on a household survey with in-home alarm testing

summary: Cross-sectional survey recommended; the decision cites claim-9.
